title: Ordinary associated graded of a flat convolution
statement: Let R be a commutative ring, and P,Q integer cochain complexes of R-modules [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] with finite decreasing filtrations by subcomplexes [def-sp-filtration]. Suppose the underlying terms, every step term and every graded term of both complexes are flat. Graded pieces and projections are the successive cokernels of [def-sp-filtered-complex-subquotients]. Give the signed total tensor [def-pc-tensor-complex-sheaves] a decreasing filtration G with G^a equal to the image of the coproduct of the tensor inclusions F^iP tensor F^(a-i)Q -> P tensor Q. Let l_ai be any lifts of these tensor inclusions to G^a. For every a there is an isomorphism e_a : coproduct_i (gr^i P tensor gr^(a-i) Q) -> gr^a G whose composite with the tensor of the two quotient projections and the i-th coprojection equals l_ai followed by the quotient projection of G. No K-flatness, derived comparison or naturality is asserted.

proof.text: Flat modules are closed under extensions: tensor a short exact sequence with flat outer terms against an injection, use flat quotient tensor injectivity for both rows and chase the kernel of the middle vertical map. Induct through the finite graded layers to show every term of P/F^i P and Q/F^j Q is flat; below the lower bound the quotient is zero, and above the upper bound it is the whole flat module.

For i+j=a project the total tensor to Tot((P/F^(i+1)P) tensor (Q/F^(j+1)Q)). On the diagonal step tensor (r,s) all components except (r,s) vanish, because r>i or s>j. There are only finitely many possibly nonzero components. Flat quotient tensor injectivity identifies the diagonal image with gr^r P tensor gr^s Q, degree by degree, and direct sums preserve these injections. Right exactness of tensor identifies the diagonal kernel with the sum of the two next-step tensor images.

Restrict the diagonal projection to G^a and factor through the direct sum of diagonal images. It is surjective by lifting representatives. It kills G^(a+1). Conversely every element in the kernel is a finite sum of diagonal step-tensor contributions; off-diagonal vanishing makes each contribution vanish separately in its graded tensor, and the diagonal kernel calculation puts it in G^(a+1). The maps commute with the signed differential. Thus the cokernel of G^(a+1)->G^a is canonically the indicated sum. Inverting that quotient isomorphism gives e_a and the representative formula. The lifts l_ai are unique by monicity of the subobject inclusions.

theorem flatConvolution_graded_iso
    (P Q : FilteredObject (CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ))
    (hPfin : P.filtration.IsFinite) (hQfin : Q.filtration.IsFinite)
    (hP : ∀ n, ObjectProperty.flat (P.obj.X n))
    (hQ : ∀ n, ObjectProperty.flat (Q.obj.X n))
    (hPs : ∀ i n, ObjectProperty.flat
      ((P.filtration.step i : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ).X n))
    (hQs : ∀ i n, ObjectProperty.flat
      ((Q.filtration.step i : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ).X n))
    (hPg : ∀ i n, ObjectProperty.flat ((P.filtration.gradedPiece i).X n))
    (hQg : ∀ i n, ObjectProperty.flat ((Q.filtration.gradedPiece i).X n))
    (G : DecreasingFiltration (P.obj ⊗ Q.obj))
    (hG : ∀ a : ℤ, G.step a = imageSubobject
      (Sigma.desc (fun i : ℤ ↦
        (P.filtration.step i).arrow ⊗ₘ (Q.filtration.step (a - i)).arrow)))
    (l : ∀ a i : ℤ,
      (P.filtration.step i : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) ⊗
          (Q.filtration.step (a - i) : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ) ⟶
        (G.step a : CochainComplex (ModuleCat.{u} R) ℤ))
    (hl : ∀ a i, l a i ≫ (G.step a).arrow =
      (P.filtration.step i).arrow ⊗ₘ (Q.filtration.step (a - i)).arrow) :
    ∀ a : ℤ, ∃ e :
      (∐ fun i : ℤ ↦ P.filtration.gradedPiece i ⊗ Q.filtration.gradedPiece (a - i)) ≅
        G.gradedPiece a,
      ∀ i : ℤ,
        (P.filtration.complexQuotientπ i (i + 1) (by omega) ⊗ₘ
          Q.filtration.complexQuotientπ (a - i) (a - i + 1) (by omega)) ≫
          Sigma.ι (fun i : ℤ ↦
            P.filtration.gradedPiece i ⊗ Q.filtration.gradedPiece (a - i)) i ≫ e.hom =
        l a i ≫ G.complexQuotientπ a (a + 1) (by omega)
